links.outcome: Hallucination detection performance of LLP-based validation versus classical symbolic validators on benchmark datasets
links.effect: LLP-based validation improved over classical symbolic validators, especially with discourse modeling. Performance on the challenging clinical narrative dataset was weaker, showing difficulty with implicit, ambiguous language. No numbers in abstract.
links.quote: Experiments on benchmark hallucination-detection datasets show that LLP-based validation improves over classical symbolic validators, especially when combined with discourse modeling, while results on a challenging clinical narrative dataset highlight the difficulty of verifying implicit, ambiguous, and underspecified patient language.

links.outcome: Human hallucination detection accuracy, interpretability, and trust with logic-assisted explanations
links.effect: Logic-assisted explanations improved hallucination detection accuracy, interpretability, and user trust in the human evaluation. No numbers reported in abstract.
links.quote: A human evaluation further indicates that logic-assisted explanations improve hallucination detection accuracy, interpretability, and user trust.

unlisted_practices: Labeled logic program (symbolic reasoning) validation layer with discourse-aware weighting to validate LLM diagnostic reasoning

screen.reason: The study introduces and evaluates a validation guardrail framework (ValidLLP4LLM) to detect hallucinations and validate reasoning in LLM-assisted clinical diagnosis, evaluating both on datasets and via a human-in-the-loop study assessing hallucination detection and clinician trust.

primary.practice: logic-based reasoning validation and hallucination detection guardrail
